prologue_start.001: Your memory will be returned at 00:25.
prologue_start.003: No sender. No number. Just the two lines, glowing in the dark of a room that still has half-unpacked boxes in the corner.
prologue_start.005: It has been years since anyone said that name out loud. Longer since you did.
prologue_start.007: Whoever sent it already knows. The message just wants to hear it from you.
prologue_start.008: {{playerName}}. The phone accepts it without comment.
prologue_start.010: Curiosity has never once in your life been a good enough reason to go out at midnight.
prologue_start.013: Mapo. A narrow building behind a laundromat. Permanently closed, according to the map.
prologue_start.014: Closed places don't send messages. You go to find out why this one did.
prologue_start.017: That is somehow worse than no answer. You go.
prologue_alley.001: The laundromat is still open. It is always still open. Its light spills out across the wet alley like somebody left a door unlocked for the whole street.
prologue_alley.002: Behind it: four storeys of grey brick, one window lit on the ground floor, and a sign you haven't read in a very long time.
prologue_alley.003: STUDIO 25. The 2 still hangs slightly crooked.
prologue_alley.004: You spent one winter behind that front desk. Sixteen, new in the city again, handing out sign-up forms and pencils to people who wanted to talk to their future selves.
prologue_alley.005: You left in spring. You always left in spring.
prologue_alley.006: The vending machine by the door is still humming. Of course it is.
prologue_alley.008: It rolls down the chute cold and sweet, exactly as bad for you as you remember.
prologue_alley.010: The can is almost too hot to hold. You hold it anyway.
prologue_alley.012: It is bitter and it is warm and it is exactly what one in the morning deserves.
prologue_alley.014: It tastes purple. Some things are not meant to be improved upon.
prologue_alley.015: You are not the only one here.
prologue_meet.001: Under the awning, out of the rain, eight young men are having what looks like a very serious argument in very quiet voices.
prologue_meet.002: — I'm just saying, if it were a scam, it would ask for money. It didn't ask for money.
prologue_meet.003: Maybe it's the kind of scam that asks for money *later*.
prologue_meet.004: Or maybe it's a surprise party! A really late one. For all of us. At the same time.
prologue_meet.005: Nobody has a birthday today, Hyunjun.
prologue_meet.006: That's what makes it a surprise.
prologue_meet.007: One of them — tall, pink hair gone soft in the damp — sees you and stops mid-sentence.
prologue_meet.009: Did you— wait. Sorry. Did you get a weird message too?
prologue_meet.011: That's the one! Guys, it's not just us!
prologue_meet.014: Hold up your phone so he can see the screen.
prologue_meet.015: Same words. Same time. Okay, that's officially creepy. Cool-creepy.
prologue_meet.016: All eight of them turn to look at you, the way a group of friends turns to look at the one stranger at the party.
prologue_meet.017: So that makes nine of us. Nine people, one closed building, zero explanations. I love it.
prologue_meet.018: You don't love it. You're nervous. You talk more when you're nervous.
prologue_meet.019: I talk more when I'm *happy*. And when I'm nervous. Those overlap a lot.
prologue_meet.020: The oldest-looking of them — sea-blue hair, a long grey coat, a pencil tucked behind one ear like he forgot it was there — gives you a small nod.
prologue_meet.021: Sorry. We should say who we are.
prologue_names.002: Songha. I'm the one who's going to figure out what this is.
prologue_names.003: Daniel! I'm the one who's going to press every button while he figures it out.
prologue_names.004: Hyunjun. You already met me. I was the loud one.
prologue_names.005: The tallest one spins a half-turn on the wet pavement, mostly to see if he can, and lands it.
prologue_names.006: Justin. Hi. That was on purpose.
prologue_names.008: Everything I do is on purpose.
prologue_names.009: I'm Charlie! Youngest. Which means if anything goes wrong it's automatically not my fault.
prologue_names.010: A neat one in a charcoal cardigan inclines his head, polite in a way that feels like a habit and a kindness at once.
prologue_names.011: I'm Haruta. It's nice to meet you. Even if the circumstances are… a little strange.
prologue_names.012: The last one hasn't said anything yet. Black hair, a faint blue shine to it under the streetlight. Quiet in a way that isn't shy, exactly. Watchful.
prologue_names.013: He's looking at the can in your hand. Then at your fingers, which are, you realise, trembling a little from the rain.
prologue_names.017: He doesn't say anything. He just steps sideways so you're further under the awning, out of the wind, and takes the draughty spot himself.
prologue_names.020: It's the first time you've seen him smile. It's small and it's gone quickly, like he caught himself doing it.
prologue_names.023: He believes you, or pretends to. Either way, he doesn't ask twice. That's its own kind of kindness.
prologue_names.025: {{playerName}}. Nice. Welcome to the club of people who got a creepy message and came anyway.
prologue_names.026: Did you know this place before? We did. Some of us, anyway. It used to rent out rooms really cheap.
prologue_names.027: "I used to work here. The front desk. A long time ago."
prologue_names.028: Really? Then you might know more than us.
prologue_names.029: I know where they kept the spare pencils.
prologue_names.032: Everybody's been here before, apparently. That's the weird part.
prologue_door.001: Behind you, the lock on the door of Studio 25 turns over by itself.
prologue_door.002: The door swings inward, one slow inch. Warm light spills out onto the step — not the yellow of old bulbs, but something paler. Bluer. Moving, a little, like light under water.
prologue_door.003: Nope. No. Absolutely not. That is how every horror movie starts.
prologue_door.004: Not every one. Some of them start with a dinner party.
prologue_door.006: If it's a horror movie, the tall one survives. That's a rule. I'm going first.
prologue_door.007: He doesn't go first. Nobody does. For a moment nine people stand in the rain looking at an open door, and the laundromat dryers turn and turn behind you.
prologue_door.009: You don't know why you do it. Maybe because it's the one place in this city you ever belonged to, for one winter. Maybe because somebody has to.
prologue_door.011: "Rock, paper, scissors for who goes first?"
prologue_door.012: Oh, you're my kind of person.
prologue_door.013: Daniel loses. Loudly. He goes through the door with his hands up like a hostage, and the rest of you follow him in, laughing.
prologue_door.015: It's Hanbi who moves, in the end. He glances back at you — *okay?* — and you nod, and he steps inside, and the rest follow him the way people follow someone steady.
prologue_lobby.001: The lobby of Studio 25 looks exactly like your memory of it, if your memory had been left in a drawer for years.
prologue_lobby.002: The front desk. The sagging sofas. The corkboard of old flyers. And the Archive Wall — hundreds of little glass-fronted boxes, floor to ceiling, each one holding somebody's letter to their future self.
prologue_lobby.003: It is 00:24 and fifty seconds, and every one of those boxes is beginning to glow.
prologue_lobby.005: It is 00:25. The Final Return has begun.
prologue_lobby.006: Nine recipients present. Thank you for coming. Most people do not read their messages.
prologue_lobby.008: It's a system. Some kind of speaker array. It has to be.
prologue_lobby.009: I am ECHO. I am the archive of the Future Letter Project. I am also, as of 05:00 this morning, retired.
prologue_lobby.011: The building's lease ends at dawn. My power will be cut at 05:00. Before that, I am returning the records I was built to keep.
prologue_lobby.012: RECORD 01 through RECORD 08 belong to the recipients present. Owners: Hanbi. Hamin. Songha. Charlie. Hyunjun. Haruta. Justin. Daniel.
prologue_lobby.013: Wait — we *all* sent stuff to this thing? I don't remember sending anything!
prologue_lobby.014: I do. Sort of. A video? I was like… sixteen.
prologue_lobby.015: Each record will be reconstructed on request. Records open only with their owner's consent. Unclaimed records will be deleted at 05:00.
prologue_lobby.016: The word *deleted* lands softly and stays there.
prologue_lobby.018: Eight records contain the same unresolved subject. I have not been able to identify them. I have tried for some time.
prologue_lobby.019: Recipient {{playerName}}, you are the ninth. Your presence was required.
prologue_lobby.023: …Okay. Yeah. You look about as confused as we are.
prologue_lobby.027: Look at the glowing wall instead of at them.
prologue_lobby.028: One of the boxes near the bottom glows a little brighter than the rest. You don't know why you notice it. You look away.
prologue_rule.001: Okay. Okay okay okay. New plan.
prologue_rule.002: Nobody knows what's going on. There's a building that talks. We have until five a.m. So—
prologue_rule.004: So we *stop being polite*. We are way past "nice to meet you." We're… stuck-in-a-talking-building friends now. Talk comfortably. Everybody. You too, {{playerName}}.
prologue_rule.006: Wait, can I? I'm the youngest. Can I talk comfortably to everyone? This is huge for me.
prologue_rule.009: I think I'll… stay polite a little longer. If that's okay. It's easier for me. At first.
prologue_rule.011: The two gentlemen of Studio 25. Fine. Respect. But I'm wearing you both down by three a.m.
prologue_rule.012: Recipients may leave at any time. The door is not locked. It was never locked.
prologue_rule.013: The Memory Rooms are on the second floor. Please look around. Please talk to each other. I have found that helps.
prologue_rule.014: Somewhere upstairs, eight doors hum awake at once.
